name: Teaflask
long_description:
Teaflask is the AI layer for software companies. It lets any SaaS company put an agent inside its product that carries out tasks for its users, with the controls enterprises require. Customers go live in a day, without a rebuild.

Calling a model is the easy part of shipping an in-product agent. The hard part is everything around it: streaming, crash recovery, scaling, guardrails, interfaces that match the product, and knowledge that stays current as the code changes. Teaflask handles all of it with no backend changes, and gives product teams visibility into how their users actually use the product.
one_liner: Make your product AI native by tomorrow.

launches.tagline: Teaflask is a managed platform for adding an agentic frontend to the SaaS product you already ship.
launches.body:
60s brainrot-style tldr: <https://youtube.com/shorts/U_kPyM4gvMs?feature=share>\
\
Hello hello, Ragav from Teaflask here!\
\
Teaflask is a managed platform for adding an agentic frontend to the SaaS product you already ship. The platform is **self-serve**, you can **bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI keys** (particularly great for companies with lots of credits!). Most of the core product is available on Free plan with generous rate limits. Paid tier is for companies who want dedicated support and SLAs.

**What it is:**\
Teaflask has two parts: a ready-to-deploy package that becomes part of your product’s frontend, and a managed platform that runs everything behind it.

The <https://github.com/teaflask/assistant>  package can appear as a full page, sidebar, corner widget or command palette.

It can:

* Answer users’ questions about your product
* Read the current page and navigate users to the right place
* Fill forms for users to review
* Call your product’s APIs on a user’s behalf
* Complete long, multi-step workflows
* Delegate background work to subagents

A particularly cool feature is: **tool views**. You can provide your own UI components for each tool, so an invoice lookup can render as an invoice component, an availability check can show a calendar etc. They can be configured to render per state (called, running, finished, failed, awaiting approval etc). See the gif below for an example.\
The managed platform behind the package provides your product knowledge (**catches stale docs!**), model runtime, action controls, approvals, conversation history, real-time streaming, durable execution and autoscaling required to make this work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=122231&key=user_uploads/1978093/eea3e622-b18e-4d27-90e7-6ddf7765e660)


**Sidenote** about the package: It’s a react package but non-react builds can import a <script> tag and get the same functionality. The default package’s UI is pretty polished and ready to deploy as is. Nevertheless you can customize its theme (or even use it headlessly if you’d rather build your own UI).

**How it works:**

* You connect your GitHub repository to Teaflask. This is optional, although you lose some important capabilities if you skip it. More on that below.\*
* Teaflask scans the codebase and does two things:
  * It helps you write documentation for your product, which you can optionally publish as a public help centre.
  * It discovers API operations and proposes an action catalogue, or agent tools, that you can set to **Allow**, **Ask** or **Deny**.
* In the Teaflask dashboard, you configure the system prompt, model, memory, actions, skills and other capabilities.
* You add the @teaflask/assistant package to your frontend and connect it to your existing API client. A coding agent can usually get the whole thing set up **in about an hour.**

At runtime, the split is fairly simple: the model and agent loop run on Teaflask’s infrastructure, while anything that needs to interact with your product happens in the user’s browser.

We manage the model-provider calls, routing, auto-summarization, guardrails, memory, subagent orchestration, streaming and durable execution. Reading the current page, navigating, filling forms and calling your API happen through the Teaflask package in the browser.

API requests use the signed-in user’s existing session. From your backend’s perspective, the request is being made by that user, through the same authentication, permissions and business logic your product already applies. You do not need to rebuild your backend or give Teaflask administrator credentials.

If a task needs approval, the run pauses and asks the user. If it takes a long time or the user closes the page, the run can resume from where it stopped.

\***What happens if you don’t want to connect your repo?**

You can choose not to connect a repository and instead write the documentation manually and upload an API specification (openapi, swagger, graphql) for Teaflask to prepare the action catalogue from. You lose two things by doing this.

* **Teaflask has a provenance engine** that checks verifiable documentation claims against your latest production code. If something stops being true as the codebase changes, Teaflask flags it and can propose a correction.
* Teaflask can rescan the codebase and **propose updates** to the action catalogue as your API changes. Without repository access, you are responsible for keeping both the documentation and API specification current.

I recommend connecting your repo. Teaflask has read-only access and the sandbox your repo is \[temporarily\] cloned into is network fenced.

**Additional features (not GA yet):**

* A testing/simulation engine where you can replay conversations and workflows. Great for **testing** if smaller/cheaper models can achieve the same outcomes, if changing the model config breaks something etc.
* Let your own users bring their own AI subscriptions.

**Asks:**\
I would especially appreciate feedback on:

* Which parts of the setup feel like too much work.
* Whether you need server-to-server API actions in addition to browser-executed ones, particularly for operations a normal end user cannot perform (a use case that has come up is if you want to build-your-own AI customer service agent; you typically don’t expose APIs like “issue refund” etc. directly to the users). If so, what authentication and approval model would you expect?

If you’re scoping Teaflask for your company, I’d love to hear from you. Please book a call using <https://cal.com/d/5ZSVqWNGvXe1MK6mEhmPjT/discovery-call>
